title: Sales Enablement Prospect Kit: Positioning, Competitive Briefs, Pitch Decks, Pricing Guidance, Case Studies & Security FAQ
author: Morgan Patel
summary: A single prospect-ready kit for SDRs/AEs and solution engineers: messages, competitive talking points, a pitch deck outline, pricing guidance, two short case studies with concrete metrics, and a security FAQ for prospect discussions.
content:
Purpose
This prospect kit consolidates the canonical positioning, competitive talking points, pitch deck outline, pricing guidance, negotiation playbook, short case studies, and a security FAQ used by Redwood Inference AEs and Solutions Engineers. Use this doc when preparing pre-sales calls, proof-of-concept (POC) scoping, and procurement discussions.

Audience
- Sales (SDRs/AEs)
- Solutions Engineering
- Customer Success (pre-sales)
- Go-to-market leadership

1) Elevator & Core Positioning
- Elevator: Redwood Inference is a developer-first inference platform that delivers predictable, cost-efficient LLM serving across hosted, dedicated, and private deployments — so engineering teams ship LLM features without rebuilding inference infra.
- Core value props (tailor by persona):
  - Engineering/Platform: Unified runtime (Redwood Runtime) with standardized APIs, continuous KV/prefix caching, and kernel selection that reduces per-token cost up to 3x vs unmanaged self-hosting.
  - Product/PM: Predictable latency & rollout controls (canary/A-B/fallback) to safely ship model upgrades without UX regressions.
  - Security/Compliance: VPC/private deployment options, KMS/HSM integrations, and SOC 2 / ISO 27001 evidence for audit readiness.

2) Positioning by Use Case (short bullets for quick reference)
- Text generation/chat for customer-facing apps: prioritize Redwood API for speed-to-value; sample metrics: p50 gen latency 120–180ms, p95 <400ms on hosted tiers.
- High-throughput batch/embedding pipelines: recommend Redwood Dedicated with autoscaling and reserved capacity for predictable unit economics.
- Regulated workloads: Redwood Private (VPC/on-prem) with customer-managed networking and optional air-gapped packaging.

3) Competitive Brief (talking points + table)
- Primary competitors to call out: Large cloud vendor managed endpoints, LLM API providers, and inference runtime vendors.
- Differentiators to emphasize: production-first SLAs, transparent perf/cost benchmarks, unified experience across hosted/dedicated/private, and built-in rollouts + quality monitoring.

Competitive snapshot (one-slide summary):
- Redwood Inference: Unified runtime; hosted/dedicated/private; 99.95% SLA for Dedicated; p50 latency targets 100–200ms for standard gen workloads; autoscaling + intelligent batching; audit evidence (SOC2/ISO).
- Cloud-managed endpoints: broad integrations but higher per-token cost and less opinionated batching; limited private deployment automation.
- LLM API-only providers: easiest to start, varying reliability and enterprise controls; may lack dedicated reserved capacity and private deployment support.
- Self-hosted runtimes: full control but long build time and higher operational risk; Redwood reduces time-to-production and ongoing ops.

4) Pitch Deck Outline (10–12 slides, core messages)
1. Title / Logo / One-line positioning
2. The problem (latency/cost/unreliability of DIY inference) — customer pain points
3. What Redwood solves (short bullets + product icons: Redwood API, Redwood Dedicated, Redwood Private, Redwood Console, Redwood Optimize)
4. How it works at a high level (serving runtime, kernel selection, smart routing, caching)
5. Performance and cost benchmarks (sample charts: tokens/sec, $/1M tokens)
6. Security & compliance (SOC2, ISO 27001, VPC/Private, KMS)
7. Deployment options & SLA matrix (Hosted vs Dedicated vs Private)
8. Case studies / outcomes (2–3 short customer stories with metrics)
9. Pricing & packaging (high-level tiers and reserved capacity options)
10. Next steps & POC offer (timeline, engineering contact)

Pitching notes: start with the buyer's primary concern — latency, cost predictability, or compliance — and map to the deployment mode. Use the bench-marking slides to quantify likely unit economics improvements.

5) Pricing Guidance & Playbook
- Pricing primitives:
  - Hosted API: usage-based pricing per token (generation / embeddings / reranking) + tiered volumes.
  - Dedicated: monthly reserved GPU capacity (committed throughput) + overage rates; typical commitments: 3–12 months.
  - Private: platform license + professional services + optional support tier; custom pricing for on-prem or air-gapped installs.
- Example pricing bands (for conversation only — reference legal/pricing team for final quotes):
  - Small Hosted: $0.0025 / 1K tokens (generation), $0.0004 / embedding unit (example)
  - Dedicated (reserved): starting $8k–$25k / month per GPU equivalent depending on model mix and burst policy
  - Private: one-time platform fee $100k–$500k + annual maintenance (varies by scope)
- Discounting playbook:
  1) Standard discount up to 15% on committed annual Hosted usage for pipeline-driven procurement.
  2) For Dedicated: use multi-quarter commitments (6–12 months) to layer in 10–25% discounts + onboarding credits.
  3) For strategic enterprise deals: engage RevOps and Legal early; escalate to Director of GTM for >$500k TCV deals.
- Pricing checklist before submitting an LOE/quote:
  - Confirm deployment mode (Hosted/Dedicated/Private).
  - Confirm expected QPS, average sequence length, and embedding batch sizes.
  - Estimate token volume per month; run unit economics model (link to internal calculator).
  - Identify required security add-ons (higher TCO).

6) Negotiation & Procurement Playbook (for AEs/SEs)
- Qualification questions (to ask in discovery):
  - What is the expected tokens/sec / QPS and median sequence length?
  - Do you have regulatory constraints (GDPR, HIPAA, SOC2)?
  - Is deployment flexibility required (VPC, on-prem)?
  - What are the required uptime and latency SLO targets?
- POC scoping steps:
  1. Scoped POC (2–4 weeks): define success criteria (latency, cost per token, throughput).
  2. Provide trial API keys and sample performance dashboard access.
  3. Collect telemetry (latency percentiles, token counts, model outputs) to evaluate quality regression.
  4. If Dedicated/Private required, provide architecture intake doc and security questionnaire.
- Approval path for enterprise discounts: AE -> Sales Ops -> RevOps -> GTM Director for exceptions.

7) Two Short Case Studies (prospect-ready summaries)
- FinTech: "Ledgerly" (pseudonym)
  - Challenge: Real-time customer support using LLMs; unpredictable latency and high cost on third-party endpoints.
  - Redwood solution: Dedicated pool with intelligent batching and prefix caching; model pinning + canary rollouts.
  - Outcome (90-day): 2.8x reduction in per-token cost vs initial managed endpoint; p95 latency improved from 980ms to 360ms; achieved customer-facing SLA of 99.6% availability.
  - Owner: SE lead (Riley Thompson) — contact riley.thompson@redwood-inference.com
- Marketplace (B2B): "CatalogCo" (pseudonym)
  - Challenge: Embedding-based semantic search at scale with variable traffic and strict data residency requirements.
  - Redwood solution: Hybrid Dedicated + Private deployment; regional routing + KMS integration.
  - Outcome (120-day): embedding throughput scaled to 3M embeddings/day; cost per embedding lowered 45% vs DIY; compliance attestation completed for EU data residency.
  - Owner: AE (Jordan Kim) — contact jordan.kim@redwood-inference.com

8) Security FAQ (approved responses for prospect calls)
Q: What compliance certifications do you have?
A: Redwood maintains SOC 2 Type II and ISO 27001 certifications. We provide compliance artifacts under NDA. HIPAA BAA available for eligible customers.

Q: How is customer data isolated on Hosted?
A: Tenant isolation is logical on hosted tiers; we provide per-tenant encryption-at-rest (AES-256) and TLS 1.2+/1.3 in transit. For strict isolation, recommend Redwood Dedicated or Redwood Private.

Q: Do you support customer-managed keys?
A: Yes. We integrate with AWS KMS, GCP KMS, and HSM-backed key stores for Private deployments. For Dedicated, we offer KMS integration for customer-managed keys in select plans.

Q: Can we deploy in our VPC or on-prem?
A: Yes. Redwood Private supports VPC-hosted control planes and optional on-prem packaging for air-gapped environments. We provide an architecture intake and an on-prem packaging checklist on request.

Q: What logging and audit capabilities are available?
A: Redwood Console provides audit logs, request tracing, and token-level cost breakdowns. For Private deployments we can ship logs to your SIEM (Splunk/Datadog) per your retention policy.

Q: How do you handle model updates and rollbacks?
A: We support canary rollouts, A/B testing, automatic fallback to pinned model variants, and automated regression alerts tied to prompt sets/evals stored in the eval-harness.

9) Demo & POC Checklist (SE runbook)
- Pre-demo prep:
  - Confirm customer's primary persona (engineer, product, security).
  - Prepare tailored slide(s): latency/cost estimates, matching deployment recommendation.
  - Provision trial API key and scoped sample project (3–5 endpoints).
- Live demo sequence:
  1. Show Redwood Console quick tour (metrics, traces, per-route costs).
  2. Run a live generation and demonstrate streaming and function-calling.
  3. Show how to configure a canary rollout and view regression alerts.
  4. Review security artifacts and deployment options.
- Post-demo deliverables:
  - Provide POC plan (timeline, owners, success criteria).
  - Share pricing estimate and statement of work (if Private).

10) Objections & Battlecards (scripted responses)
- "We can host ourselves cheaper" -> Response: quantify total cost of ownership (engineering hours, SRE ops, time-to-market) and show unit economics from our benchmark suite; offer a 6-week POC to prove production readiness.
- "We need on-prem / air-gapped" -> Response: Redwood Private is explicitly designed for that; outline the intake and packaging timeline (8–12 weeks typical).
- "We need stronger compliance" -> Response: Provide SOC2/ISO artifacts under NDA; offer a security scoping call with our security architect.

11) Attachments & Next Steps
- Canonical assets: enterprise deck, quickstart one-pager, pricing calculator link, security questionnaire template.
- Recommended next step for most mid-market prospects: 2-week scoped POC -> performance report -> optional Dedicated commitment.

12) Ownership & Escalation
- Kit owner: Morgan Patel (GTM)
- Security artifact owner: Jordan Kim (Security liaison to GTM)
- Pricing escalation: Sales Ops -> RevOps -> GTM Director (for discounts > 15% or TCV > $500k)

Appendix A: Sample CLI snippet to demo generation (for SEs)

\curl -X POST https://api.redwood-inference.com/v1/generate \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer <PROSPECT_TRIAL_KEY>" \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d '{"model": "redwood-2b-gen", "input": "Summarize the user's request in one sentence.", "max_tokens": 60}'

Appendix B: Quick reference SLA & Perf targets
- Hosted API: best-effort; target p50 120–250ms depending on model.
- Dedicated: SLA 99.95% availability; target p50 80–200ms, p95 <350ms (depends on model family).
- Private: availability depends on customer infra; Redwood provides deployment runbooks and recommended SLOs.
